```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

# How to edit this deck
# - Slide text is plain markdown: change it directly below.
# - Numbers come from the analysis as inline R (num$usual_share and so on, listed in
#   report/numbers.R), so they stay correct when the data changes. Keep them inline instead of
#   typing the values.
# - Figures come from report/plots.R; the look from report/theme.scss.
# - Building blocks: "::: {.kpi}" big number, ":::: {.cards}" cards, ":::: {.columns}" two columns.

# FALSE: renders in seconds without data, numbers show as "…" and figures as placeholders.
# TRUE: fills in the numbers and figures from the analysis. Needs the data in data/ (see the README).
use_analysis <- TRUE

knitr::opts_chunk$set(dev = "ragg_png", dpi = 200)
source("report/numbers.R")

if (use_analysis) {
  for (f in c("setup", "load_data", "cleanup", "pupil_table", "direct_path", "stage1",
              "explained_variance", "cv_models", "goals", "conclusions")) {
    source(file.path("R", paste0(f, ".R")))
  }
  source("report/plots.R")
  has_frutiger <- any(grepl("frutiger", systemfonts::system_fonts()$family, ignore.case = TRUE))
  report_font <- register_report_font(if (has_frutiger) "Frutiger Next Pro" else "Open Sans")
  num <- report_numbers()
} else {
  num <- placeholder_numbers()
}

figure <- function(fun, placeholder) {
  if (use_analysis) print(get(fun)()) else cat(paste0("*[Figure: ", placeholder, "]*\n"))
}
# Speaker notes: the notebook's written conclusion behind a slide
notes <- function(fun) if (use_analysis) cat(get(fun)(), "\n")
```

## Time in kindergarten is hardly related to group 3 results, while early skills and support needs are {.answer}

:::: {.cards}
::: {.card}
[1]{.card-number}

**Time in kindergarten**

Children who spent more time in kindergarten have similar Cito scores in group 3. Six extra
months would add at most `r num$max_gain` SD.
:::

::: {.card}
[2]{.card-number}

**Early skills**

Skills at the end of kindergarten, especially hearing sounds and engagement, say more about how
children do in group 3.
:::

::: {.card}
[3]{.card-number}

**Scoring the learning goals**

The two classes score the same learning goals differently, which makes them hard to compare.
:::
::::

## Het Epos wants to know if a longer kindergarten or a stronger focus on group 3 goals helps pupils later on

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="33%"}
**Situation**

- Het Epos is a primary school working with children from Zuidwijk, Rotterdam
- Children start kindergarten from age 4; schools have different birth date cut-offs
- Depending on when a child is born, they spend more or less time in kindergarten
- Het Epos uses a January cut-off to offer children as much time in school as possible
:::

::: {.column width="33%"}
**Complication**

- Unequal time: children born in autumn get less time in groups 1-2
- It is unclear which areas of knowledge teachers should focus on
- Decisions and funding need evidence on whether admitting children earlier is beneficial and
  feasible
:::

::: {.column width="33%"}
**Request**

- **Time:** does a longer kindergarten help children's development and results in groups 3 and 4?
- **Focus:** does teaching towards the group 3 goals improve later results?
- **Priority:** which of the two matters more?
:::
::::

## We linked each pupil's kindergarten data to their group 3 results {.nostretch}

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4
figure("slide_diagram", "kindergarten factors, readiness and group 3 outcomes")
```

## How long a child stays in kindergarten mostly depends on their birth date

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
::: {.kpi}
[`r num$usual_share`]{.kpi-value}

[of pupils moved to group 3 in the year they turned `r num$usual_age`]{.kpi-caption}
:::

- Children start on their 4th birthday and move to group 3 in the August of the year they turn
  `r num$usual_age` (the January cut-off), so children born in autumn get the least time.
- `r num$n_moved` of the `r num$n_reached` pupils moved up a year earlier or later than their age
  group.
- This means that in our data, time in kindergarten and age are almost the same thing.
:::

::: {.column width="60%"}
```{r}
#| fig-width: 6.4
#| fig-height: 5.2
figure("slide_time_by_birth", "months in kindergarten by birth month")
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
```{r}
#| output: asis
notes("conclusion_timing")
```
:::

## Pupils who spent more time in kindergarten do not have higher Cito scores in group 3

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
::: {.kpi}
[`r num$max_gain` SD]{.kpi-value}

[the largest gain from six extra months that still fits our data, which would be a small
effect]{.kpi-caption}
:::

- For the `r num$n_cito` pupils with Cito results, scores in maths, reading speed and spelling
  were slightly lower for pupils with more time in kindergarten.
- None of the `r num$n_direct` comparisons we made showed a clear difference.
:::

::: {.column width="60%"}
```{r}
#| fig-width: 6.4
#| fig-height: 5.6
figure("slide_direct_scatter", "Cito score by months in kindergarten")
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
```{r}
#| output: asis
notes("conclusion_direct")
```
:::

## Children who take sport and movement lessons have somewhat higher Cito scores in group 3

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- **Sport & movement:** higher scores in maths, reading speed and spelling.
- **Life skills & play:** lower scores in maths.
- **Arts & culture:** lower scores in reading speed.
- **Technology, science & strategy:** needed support less often.
- Families choose these lessons themselves, so other differences between families may play a
  role.
- We tested many combinations, so a single result can be chance.
:::

::: {.column width="60%"}
```{r}
#| fig-width: 6.4
#| fig-height: 4.6
figure("slide_lessons", "each kind of lesson against the group 3 outcomes")
```
:::
::::

## Class 1/2b gives higher maths readiness scores, but its pupils score the same on Cito

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
::: {.kpi}
[`r num$class_ready_sd` SD]{.kpi-value}

[difference in maths readiness between class 1/2b and 1/2a, as scored by the
teachers]{.kpi-caption}
:::

- In group 3, pupils from both classes have about the same Cito scores.
- This suggests that the classes score the learning goals differently.
- Because of this, we compared readiness within each class.
:::

::: {.column width="60%"}
```{r}

```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}

```{r}
notes("conclusion_goals_q2")
```
:::

## Hearing sounds and engagement are the early skills most related to group 3 results

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- Hearing sounds (auditory development) covers things like rhyming and hearing the first sound of
  a word, which matter for reading and spelling.
- Engagement is how involved a child is in class activities.
- Time in kindergarten was picked in only `r num$time_kept_min`-`r num$time_kept_max`% of the
  models.
:::

::: {.column width="60%"}
```{r}
#| fig-width: 6.4
#| fig-height: 5
figure("slide_skills", "how often each skill is picked")
```
:::
::::

## Kindergarten data cannot reliably predict how an individual child will do in group 3

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
::: {.kpi}
[`r num$best_prediction`]{.kpi-value}

[of the differences in `r num$best_prediction_test` we could predict for new pupils, in the best
case]{.kpi-caption}
:::

- For the pupils used to build the models, they explained `r num$in_sample_min`-`r num$in_sample_max`.
  For new pupils this dropped a lot.
- The observations are more useful for spotting children who may need extra attention.
:::

::: {.column width="60%"}
```{r}
#| fig-width: 6.4
#| fig-height: 3.8
figure("slide_prediction", "explained share, fitted pupils and new pupils")
```
:::
::::

## We recommend four steps for the school

:::: {.cards}
::: {.card}
[1]{.card-number}

**Time in kindergarten**

A longer kindergarten is unlikely to improve Cito results. It may still help social-emotional and
gross motor development.
:::

::: {.card}
[2]{.card-number}

**Scoring**

Agree on shared scoring rules for the learning goals in both classes.
:::

::: {.card}
[3]{.card-number}

**Key skills**

Keep a close eye on hearing sounds and engagement in the last year of kindergarten.
:::

::: {.card}
[4]{.card-number}

**Support**

Use support needs in kindergarten to plan extra attention in group 3.
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
```{r}
#| output: asis
notes("recommendations_overview")
```
:::

## Our results have some limitations

:::: {.cards .cards-3}
::: {.card}
**Small sample**

`r num$n_reached` pupils reached group 3 and `r num$n_cito` have Cito results, so only larger
differences can be found.
:::

::: {.card}
**Time and age**

Time in kindergarten and age move together, so we cannot separate them.
:::

::: {.card}
**Moving up early or late**

The school decided which children moved up earlier or later, which may affect the results.
:::

::: {.card}
**Teacher observations**

Readiness scores come from each class's own teachers.
:::

::: {.card}
**Associations only**

We can show which things go together, but we cannot say what causes what.
:::
::::

## Early skills and support needs say more about group 3 results than time in kindergarten {.closing background-color="#F6A70A"}
